findings.claim: The new CAUTION block says the Operator will fail unless the `rolling-updates` feature is enabled, but the operator never checks the feature. Either the documented gate is missing from the operator, or the docs are false.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "ROLLING_UPDATES\|rolling-updates" operator/src/main` finds nothing. UpgradeLogicFactory.create (UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) picks the logic from UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy alone. KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:122-124 only passes spec.features through to the server. UpgradeTest.java:104-106 still runs with null features through createInitialDeployment(null). The UpgradeTest change at 110-115 only enables the feature for the server and tests no operator gate. Suggested red test: an operator test that sets spec.update.strategy with no features.enabled and expects failure; today it would not fail. All seats reasoned this; none ran it.
findings.reason: Three seats agree, including both correctness seats. One decision is needed first: add an operator gate (red test: CR with spec.update and no feature must fail) or remove the sentence from the docs. ponytail noted it only outside its role and excluded it from its findings, so it is not counted.

findings.claim: testFeatureNotEnabled checks only the error message. It never asserts the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code 4.
findings.evidence: The file has no assertEquals(4, ...exitCode()). The only exit-code assertion is assertEquals(0, ...) at line 75. The tests are @RawDistOnly, so result.exitCode() is available (testCompatible already uses it). CompatibilityResult.java:34-35 assigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Severity normalised to Minor because this is a missing assertion, not a code defect; superpowers rated its combined exit-code test gap Important. The fix is the assertion itself.

findings.claim: The feature-off path is tested only for `metadata`. The separate copy of the gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is never exercised with the feature disabled.
findings.evidence: The @Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME}) call is the only launch without ENABLE_FEATURE. The guard at UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50 has no test with the feature off.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Add a `check` launch without the feature that asserts the error and exit code 4.

findings.claim: The same 5-line feature gate (isFeatureEnabled, printFeatureDisabled, exit(FEATURE_DISABLED), return) is copied into both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() (46-50) instead of living once in AbstractUpdatesCommand.
findings.evidence: The two blocks are identical in the diff. `grep -rn printFeatureDisabled --include=*.java .` shows only the definition (AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:83-85) and the two copies. Both classes extend AbstractUpdatesCommand. Behaviour is unchanged, so no test fails.
findings.reason: Three seats agree; mattpocock raised it as a 'possible duplicated code' smell. The fix is a minimal consolidation: one helper in AbstractUpdatesCommand that each run() calls. This is not a speculative abstraction.

findings.claim: The recreate exit code was renumbered from 4 to 3, but no test asserts it. testIncompatible checks only the error text.
findings.evidence: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 (CompatibilityResult.java:34-35). Lines 88-107 have no exit-code assertion. If the two values were later swapped, no test would fail.
findings.reason: Raised by only two seats, so it is below the main-list threshold. superpowers rated it Important; normalised to Minor as a test gap.

findings.claim: The exit-code table describes 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible'. That mixes up 'feature disabled' with a compatibility verdict, and it omits that `metadata` returns the same code.
findings.evidence: UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50 (48) also exits with FEATURE_DISABLED. Scripts that treat a non-zero `check` result as 'recreate' would recreate when the feature is simply off.
findings.reason: Raised by only two seats, so it is below the main-list threshold.

findings.claim: Renumbering the recreate exit code from 4 to 3, and reusing 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, is an unannounced behaviour change bundled into the feature-flag change.
findings.evidence: The base docs already said 3, so the change aligns code with docs. The command is unreleased and preview (added in 588e60e058, version 999.0.0-SNAPSHOT). Scripts written against the old behaviour would read 'feature disabled' as 'recreate'. Both seats say it deserves a mention in the PR or a release/migration note.
findings.reason: Raised by only two seats, so it is below the main-list threshold.

findings.claim: The constant FEATURE_DISABLED drops the _EXIT_CODE suffix that its siblings use.
findings.evidence: The siblings are ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE.
findings.reason: Raised by one advisory seat as a 'possible mysterious name' smell, so it is below the main-list threshold.

findings.claim: The commit history breaches CONTRIBUTING.md. There are 5 commits ('feedback', 'fix test failure', and so on), and only the first ends with 'Closes #36840'.
findings.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md requires one commit per PR, with the issue link as the last line. The breach goes away if the PR is squashed on merge.
findings.reason: Raised by one advisory seat, so it is below the main-list threshold. It is about commit history, not a file.

findings.claim: There is no release-note entry for the new preview feature (Profile.java:136) or for the CLI behaviour change (the command now requires --features=rolling-updates).
findings.evidence: PR-CHECKLIST.md asks for release notes 'if applicable', and nothing was found under docs/documentation/release_notes. Whether it applies is arguable, because the command is unreleased.
findings.reason: Raised by one advisory seat, so it is below the main-list threshold.

findings.claim: The shared operator test image is now built with the rolling-updates preview feature, so every operator test that uses the custom image runs with it, not just UpgradeTest.
findings.evidence: build-testing-docker-images.sh:12 builds this one image for the whole suite. BaseOperatorTest.getTestKeycloakDeployment applies customImage to every deployment. Impact is low today, since the feature changes nothing beyond the CLI gate.
findings.reason: Raised by only two seats, so it is below the main-list threshold.

findings.claim: The macro hard-codes --features=rolling-updates after the user's parameters. This overrides features the user set through KC_FEATURES or keycloak.conf. With --optimized images, a runtime --features flag may not take effect, and the guide never says the feature must be part of the build.
findings.evidence: CLI options take priority over env and config files, which conflicts with the guide's rule to 'include all configuration options'. Commits b1965bb9c4 ('do not use custom image, it fails') and 5d2490d33a (bakes the feature into the image) point the same way. The --optimized behaviour was reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Raised by one seat, so it is below the main-list threshold. The --optimized claim is unverified.

coverage: Files skipped: none.
